title: Complete Graphic Design Program: Canva & Adobe Photoshop
description: A full 18-module graphic design program: design fundamentals, Canva (basics to advanced), Adobe Photoshop, logo & brand identity, print, photo manipulation, advertising, AI tools, freelancing, 20 real-world projects, a professional portfolio and a Certificate of Completion.
outcomes: Master design fundamentals: principles, colour, typography and layout
Design confidently in Canva (basics, advanced, social & marketing)
Edit and create in Adobe Photoshop (editing, tools, manipulation)
Design logos, full brand identities and print-ready materials
Create advertising, social media and marketing graphics
Use AI design tools, build a portfolio and start freelancing
about: This is the complete TIH Graphic Design Program, rebuilt into eighteen modules covering Canva and Adobe Photoshop from beginner to professional.

Every content lesson has a video and printable notes; twenty real-world projects and a capstone build your portfolio, and you learn logo/branding, print, photo manipulation, advertising, AI tools and freelancing.

Software used: Canva (Free & Pro), Adobe Photoshop and Adobe Firefly (AI), with free assets from Google Fonts, Freepik, Unsplash and Pexels. You finish with a portfolio and — after the graduation assessment — a Certificate of Completion.
requirements: A computer or tablet with internet access
A free Canva account (Photoshop optional/trial for those modules)
Willingness to practise every design in Canva or Photoshop

faqs.question: Do I need artistic talent to take this course?
faqs.answer: Not at all. Graphic design is a learnable skill. This course teaches you the principles and tools that make design systematic, not just talent-based.

faqs.question: Is Canva free?
faqs.answer: Canva has a free version that covers most of this course. We also use some Canva Pro features (available free with a 30-day trial). Professional accounts cost about $13/month.

faqs.question: Do I need to buy Photoshop?
faqs.answer: Adobe Photoshop requires a subscription (about $21/month) but Adobe offers a free 7-30 day trial which is sufficient to complete the course modules.

faqs.question: Can I make money with graphic design in Liberia?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. Liberian businesses, churches, NGOs, and political campaigns constantly need flyers, social media graphics, and brand identities. Freelance design income is very achievable.

instructor.name: Patricia Sumo
instructor.title: Creative Director & Brand Design Specialist
instructor.bio: Patricia Sumo is a creative director with over 10 years of design experience working with brands across Liberia, Ghana, and Nigeria. She founded Sumo Creative Studio and has trained hundreds of designers at TIH Academy.

lessons.html:
Graphic Design · Module 1Canva · Adobe Photoshop

Key Words & Meanings

Welcome to the Course

Welcome to the Course is the focus of this Course Orientation lesson. It develops the learner’s ability to make, explain, and refine visual decisions that serve a real audience and purpose.

Graphic design

The practice of communicating ideas and information through intentional visual form.

brief

A document defining the design purpose, audience, message, deliverables, constraints, and deadline.

workspace

The physical and digital arrangement of tools, files, panels, and settings used for design work.

🧭 Welcome to the Course
Understand the visual principle, study the example, build your own design, and improve it through critique.

Welcome to the Course

Definition

Welcome to the Course is a practical part of Course Orientation: the purpose, tools, careers, workflow, and learning path of professional visual communication. It is successful when the intended viewer understands the message and can take the intended action.

Detailed explanation

Graphic design is visual communication, not decoration alone. For Welcome to the Course, begin with purpose, audience, message, format, and viewing conditions. Those facts determine the hierarchy, layout, type, colours, imagery, and level of detail.

A professional designer creates more than one possible direction, checks the work at its real size, asks for specific feedback, and keeps the source editable. Every visual decision should have a reason connected to the brief.

Step-by-step design workflow

  1. Clarify the purpose and audience.
  2. Prepare Canva, Photoshop, folders, fonts, and export locations.
  3. Create a small design, review it, and save the editable source.

Understanding the visual example

The large headline creates the first level of hierarchy. The smaller supporting line provides context without competing. Alignment gives the composition order, white space separates information, and the accent colour highlights a controlled focal point. The same principles apply whether the final work is a flyer, logo, social post, photograph, presentation, or brand system.

Visual critique: what to check

Design questionProfessional standard
What is noticed first?The most important message has the strongest hierarchy.
Is everything readable?Type size, contrast, line length, and spacing suit the final viewing condition.
Does the layout feel organised?Elements align to a grid and related information is grouped.
Is every element necessary?Decoration that does not support the message is removed.

Canva or Photoshop practice

  1. Create the correct canvas size and save the source with a clear project name.
  2. Build the main hierarchy using only text, simple shapes, and one image.
  3. Apply Welcome to the Course deliberately and keep important edits non-destructive.
  4. Review at final size, proofread, and compare with the brief.
  5. Export the correct format and keep the editable source separately.
🎨 Practical task: Make a small design demonstrating Welcome to the Course. Produce two variations, ask one person which communicates better and why, then revise the stronger version and save it for your portfolio.

Export and delivery checklist

  • Correct dimensions, orientation, resolution, and colour mode.
  • Names, dates, prices, contacts, spelling, and logo use checked.
  • Readable on the actual phone, screen, or printed size.
  • Source file organised; final files named clearly.
  • Usage rights confirmed for fonts, photographs, icons, and AI assets.

Summary

Welcome to the Course belongs to Course Orientation. A professional result communicates one clear purpose, uses intentional hierarchy and craft, survives real-size testing, and is delivered in the correct editable and final formats.

Design habit: Zoom out or hold the work at arm’s length. If the main message is not immediately clear, strengthen the hierarchy before adding more decoration.

Design questionProfessional standard

A professional designer creates more than one possible direction, checks the work at its real size, asks for specific feedback, and keeps the source editable. Every visual decision should have a reason connected to the brief.

Professional design brief

Create Portfolio Submission for a realistic Liberian or African business, school, church, NGO, event, or creator. Define the audience, message, size, delivery channel, deadline, and approval criteria before opening Canva or Photoshop.

Required deliverables

  • Written brief and two initial concepts or sketches.
  • Editable Canva or PSD source file with organised layers.
  • Correctly sized final PNG, JPG, PDF, or platform format.
  • A realistic mockup showing the design in use.
  • A short design rationale explaining hierarchy, colour, typography, imagery, and revisions.

Step-by-step design workflow

  1. Approve the brief, research plan, milestones, and deliverables.
  2. Develop concepts, document critique, and refine the selected direction.
  3. Present final applications and explain decisions using evidence.

Understanding the visual example

The large headline creates the first level of hierarchy. The smaller supporting line provides context without competing. Alignment gives the composition order, white space separates information, and the accent colour highlights a controlled focal point. The same principles apply whether the final work is a flyer, logo, social post, photograph, presentation, or brand system.

Visual critique: what to check

Design questionProfessional standard
What is noticed first?The most important message has the strongest hierarchy.
Is everything readable?Type size, contrast, line length, and spacing suit the final viewing condition.
Does the layout feel organised?Elements align to a grid and related information is grouped.
Is every element necessary?Decoration that does not support the message is removed.

Canva or Photoshop practice

  1. Create the correct canvas size and save the source with a clear project name.
  2. Build the main hierarchy using only text, simple shapes, and one image.
  3. Apply Portfolio Submission deliberately and keep important edits non-destructive.
  4. Review at final size, proofread, and compare with the brief.
  5. Export the correct format and keep the editable source separately.
🎨 Practical task: Make a small design demonstrating Portfolio Submission. Produce two variations, ask one person which communicates better and why, then revise the stronger version and save it for your portfolio.

Export and delivery checklist

  • Correct dimensions, orientation, resolution, and colour mode.
  • Names, dates, prices, contacts, spelling, and logo use checked.
  • Readable on the actual phone, screen, or printed size.
  • Source file organised; final files named clearly.
  • Usage rights confirmed for fonts, photographs, icons, and AI assets.

Summary

Portfolio Submission belongs to Capstone Project. A professional result communicates one clear purpose, uses intentional hierarchy and craft, survives real-size testing, and is delivered in the correct editable and final formats.

Design habit: Zoom out or hold the work at arm’s length. If the main message is not immediately clear, strengthen the hierarchy before adding more decoration.
